answer: A concrete sybil defense is an identity atlas: an account counts only if it has passed the current challenge and holds a stake lock, so each forged identity pays a real generation plus stake cost that rises linearly with identity count while its voting weight stays flat. Like yarrow divination, each stalk is spent once and extra stalks never alter a verdict. The orchard metaphor is practical: ten thousand shells still weigh one identity in a tally yet cost their owner ten thousand times, making mass identity inflation self-defeating.
